actual_title: Civil and Political Rights in International Law
seo_title: Civil and Political Rights in International Law
excerpt: Civil and political rights protect life, liberty, security, political participation, fair trial, equality, privacy, expression, assembly, association, and freedom from torture, slavery, arbitrary detention, and abusive emergency power. This article explains civil and political rights in international law through the ICCPR, Human Rights Committee practice, regional systems, customary law, limitations, derogations, remedies, and state responsibility. It examines the right to life, humane treatment, due process, detention, protest, speech, religion, privacy, democratic participation, minority rights, non-discrimination, counterterrorism, border control, occupation, extraterritorial jurisdiction, surveillance, digital governance, and contemporary authoritarianism. By connecting doctrine, institutions, case studies, and lawyer-facing workflows, it shows how civil and political rights restrain public power while remaining contested by security claims, selective enforcement, emergency politics, and unequal access to remedies across national, regional, and international legal systems today.
